Write a Bash script that reads a list of URLs from urls.txt, downloads each with curl showing a progress bar, retries up to 3 times on failure, and stores the HTTP status code of each request in a CSV file called download_status.csv.
command:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
printf 'url,status\n' > download_status.csv
while IFS= read -r url; do
  attempts=0
  while ((attempts<3)); do
    ((attempts++))
    code=$(curl -w "%{http_code}" -L -s -S --progress-bar "$url" -o "$(basename "$url")" 2>/dev/null)
    if [[ $code -ge 200 && $code -lt 400 ]]; then
      printf '%s,%s\n' "$url" "$code" >> download_status.csv
      break
    fi
  done
  if ((attempts==3)); then
    printf '%s,FAIL\n' "$url" >> download_status.csv
  fi
done < urls.txt

Write a Bash script that rotates log files in /var/log/myapp/ daily: compress yesterday's log (myapp.log.YYYY-MM-DD) with gzip, delete compressed logs older than 30 days, and ensure a fresh myapp.log is created with correct permissions.
command:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
logdir=/var/log/myapp
yesterday=$(date -d yesterday +%F)
logfile=myapp.log
# Rotate
if [ -f "$logdir/$logfile" ]; then
  mv "$logdir/$logfile" "$logdir/${logfile}.$yesterday"
  gzip "$logdir/${logfile}.$yesterday"
fi
# Create new log file with proper perms

# Cleanup old archives

  if dpkg -s "$pkg" &>/dev/null; then
    echo "$(date +%F_%T) ALREADY_INSTALLED $pkg" >> /var/log/pkg_install.log
  else
    if apt-get install -y "$pkg"; then

      echo "$(date +%F_%T) FAILED $pkg" >> /var/log/pkg_install.log

  fi
done < packages.txt

command:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
while IFS= read -r url; do
  attempts=0
  while ((attempts<3)); do
    resp=$(curl -s -w "%{http_code}\t%{size_download}\n" -o /dev/null --max-time 10 "$url")
    code=$(echo "$resp" | cut -f1)
    size=$(echo "$resp" | cut -f2)
    if [[ $code -ge 200 && $code -lt 400 ]]; then
      echo -e "$url\t$code\t$size" >> results.tsv
      break
    else
      ((attempts++))
    fi
  done
done < urls.txt

#!/usr/bin/env bash
json_file="urls.json"
output_dir="/tmp/downloads"
mkdir -p "$output_dir"
report="download_report_$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S).csv"
echo "URL,Status,Size" > "$report"
jq -r '.[]' "$json_file" | while read -r url; do
  fname=$(basename "$url")
  outfile="$output_dir/$fname"
  http_status=$(curl -L --retry 3 --retry-delay 2 --max-time 10 -w "%{http_code}" -o "$outfile" "$url")
  size=$(stat -c "%s" "$outfile" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
  echo "\"$url\",$http_status,$size" >> "$report"
done

docker ps -a --filter "status=exited" --format "{{.Names}} {{.CreatedAt}}" |
  while read name created; do
    created_ts=$(date -d "$created" +%s)
    now_ts=$(date +%s)
    age=$(( (now_ts - created_ts) / 86400 ))
    if (( age > 48 )); then
      echo -n "Remove container $name (stopped $age days ago)? [y/N] "
      read -r answer
      if [[ $answer == [Yy]* ]]; then
        docker rm "$name"
      fi
    fi
  done

  while IFS= read -r -d '' link; do
    target=$(readlink "$link")
    if [[ ! -e "$target" ]]; then
      base=$(basename "$target")
      new="/usr/bin/$base"
      if [[ -e "$new" ]]; then
        ln -sf "$new" "$link"
        echo "Repointed $link -> $new"
      else
        rm "$link"
        echo "Removed dangling link $link"
      fi
    fi
  done

prompt: Write a script that monitors the size of /var/lib/mysql, and when it exceeds 80% of the available disk space on its partition, automatically creates a compressed snapshot of the database directory (excluding .ibd files) and uploads it to an S3 bucket using awscli, then sends a summary email via mailx.
command:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
mountpoint=$(df /var/lib/mysql | tail -1 | awk '{print $6}')
avail=$(df "$mountpoint" | tail -1 | awk '{print $4}')
used=$(du -s /var/lib/mysql | awk '{print $1}')
if (( used * 100 / avail > 80 )); then
  snap="/tmp/mysql_snapshot_$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S).tar.gz"
  tar --exclude='*.ibd' -czf "$snap" -C /var/lib mysql
  aws s3 cp "$snap" s3://my-backup-bucket/mysql/ --storage-class STANDARD_IA
  echo "MySQL snapshot uploaded: $snap" | mailx -s "MySQL Disk Usage Alert" admin@example.com
  rm -f "$snap"
fi

prompt: Provide a Bash function that takes a directory and a file extension, computes the SHA256 hash of each matching file, stores the hashes in a .sha256 file next to each original, and verifies the integrity of all files, printing any mismatches.
command:
hash_check(){
  dir="$1"
  ext="$2"
  find "$dir" -type f -name "*.$ext" | while read -r f; do
    sha256sum "$f" > "${f}.sha256"
  done
  echo "Verification results:"
  find "$dir" -type f -name "*.$ext.sha256" | while read -r h; do
    orig="${h%.sha256}"
    if ! sha256sum -c "$h" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      echo "MISMATCH: $orig"
    fi
  done
}
# Usage: hash_check /etc conf

#!/usr/bin/env bash
log=/var/log/user_create.log
while IFS=, read -r user uid; do
  if id "$user" &>/dev/null; then
    echo "$(date): $user already exists" >> "$log"
    continue
  fi
  if useradd -u "$uid" -G sudo "$user"; then

    echo "$(date): Failed to create $user" >> "$log"
  fi

prompt: Create a Bash function that monitors a given directory for new files (using inotifywait), and when a new file appears, computes its MD5 checksum, appends the filename and checksum to /var/log/file_checksums.log, and moves the file to an archive directory preserving the original subdirectory structure.

watch_new(){
  watch_dir="$1"
  archive_dir="/var/archive"
  mkdir -p "$archive_dir"
  inotifywait -m -e create --format "%w%f" "$watch_dir" | while read -r newfile; do
    checksum=$(md5sum "$newfile" | awk '{print $1}')
    echo "$(date +%F_%T) $newfile $checksum" >> /var/log/file_checksums.log
    rel=${newfile#${watch_dir}/}
    dest="$archive_dir/$(dirname "$rel")"
    mkdir -p "$dest"
    mv "$newfile" "$dest/"
  done
}
# Usage: watch_new /var/incoming

#!/usr/bin/env bash
max=$((100*1024*1024))
while :; do
  size=$(stat -c%s /var/log/syslog)
  if (( size > max )); then
    mv /var/log/syslog /var/log/syslog.1
    gzip /var/log/syslog.1
    kill -HUP $(pidof rsyslogd)
  fi
  sleep 60

prompt: Write a script that monitors a MySQL table "jobs" for new rows (poll every 10s), processes each row by calling an external API, marks the row as processed, and logs failures.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
while :; do
  rows=$(mysql -N -B -e "SELECT id, payload FROM jobs WHERE processed=0 LIMIT 10;")
  [[ -z $rows ]] && sleep 10 && continue
  while read -r id payload; do
    response=$(curl -s -X POST -d "$payload" https://api.example.com/handle)
    if [[ $response == *"success"* ]]; then
      mysql -e "UPDATE jobs SET processed=1 WHERE id=$id;"
      echo "$(date): Processed $id" >> job.log
    else
      echo "$(date): Failed $id - $response" >> job_error.log
    fi
  done <<< "$rows"
  sleep 1
done

#!/usr/bin/env bash
consec=0
while true; do
  usage=$(mpstat 1 1 | awk '/Average/ {print 100 - $NF}')
  ts=$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')
  if (( $(echo "$usage > 80" | bc -l) )); then
    echo "$ts CPU $usage%" >> /var/log/high_cpu.log
    ((consec++))
    if ((consec>=3)); then
      mail -s "High CPU Alert" admin@example.com <<EOF
CPU usage exceeded 80% for 3 consecutive checks.
Last reading: $ts ($usage%)
EOF
      consec=0
    fi
  else
    consec=0
  fi
  sleep 5
done

#!/usr/bin/env bash
terminate_oldest(){
  local pattern="$1"
  pid=$(ps -eo pid,etime,comm --no-headers |\
        awk -v pat="$pattern" '$3 ~ pat {print $1,$2}' |\
        sort -k2 | head -n1 | cut -d' ' -f1)
  [[ -z $pid ]] && return 1
  kill -TERM "$pid"
  for i in {1..10}; do
    kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null || break
    sleep 1
done
  kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null && kill -KILL "$pid"
}
# Usage: terminate_oldest "myservice"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
mapfile -t urls < urls.txt
declare -A results
for url in "${urls[@]}"; do
  fname=$(basename "$url")
  attempts=0
  until curl -L -o "$fname" "$url"; do
    ((attempts++))
    ((attempts==3)) && echo "Failed $url" && break
    sleep $((attempts*2))
  done
  if [[ -f "$fname" ]]; then
    hash=$(md5sum "$fname" | awk '{print $1}')
    results["$url"]="$hash"
  fi
done
printf '{\n' > results.json
for k in "${!results[@]}"; do
  printf '  "%s": "%s"%s\n' "$k" "${results[$k]}" "," >> results.json
done
sed -i '$ s/,$//' results.json
printf '}\n' >> results.json

prompt: Write a Bash script that monitors disk usage of /home, and when usage exceeds 80%, automatically moves the oldest files (by modification time) from /home/user/Downloads to /archive until usage drops below 70%, logging each move.
command:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
THRESH_HIGH=80
THRESH_LOW=70
while :; do
  usage=$(df --output=pcent /home | tail -1 | tr -dc '0-9')
  if (( usage > THRESH_HIGH )); then
    while (( usage > THRESH_LOW )); do
      oldest=$(find /home/user/Downloads -type f -printf '%T@ %p\n' | sort -n | head -1 | cut -d' ' -f2-)
      [ -z "$oldest" ] && break
      mv "$oldest" /archive/ && echo "$(date +'%F %T') Moved $oldest to /archive" >> /var/log/disk_cleanup.log
      usage=$(df --output=pcent /home | tail -1 | tr -dc '0-9')
    done
  fi
  sleep 300
done

Write a Bash script that reads a list of package names from packages.txt, checks if each is installed (using dpkg or rpm depending on distro), installs missing ones via apt or yum, logs each action to /var/log/pkg_install.log, and sends a summary email at the end.
command:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
log=/var/log/pkg_install.log
summary=""
while read -r pkg; do
  if command -v dpkg >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    dpkg -l "$pkg" &>/dev/null && installed=1 || installed=0
    installer='apt-get install -y'
  elif command -v rpm >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    rpm -q "$pkg" &>/dev/null && installed=1 || installed=0
    installer='yum install -y'
  else
    echo "Unsupported distro" | tee -a "$log"
    exit 1
  fi
  if (( installed )); then
    echo "$(date) INFO: $pkg already installed" | tee -a "$log"
    summary+="$pkg: already installed\n"
  else
    if $installer "$pkg"; then
      echo "$(date) INFO: $pkg installed successfully" | tee -a "$log"
      summary+="$pkg: installed\n"
    else
      echo "$(date) ERROR: failed to install $pkg" | tee -a "$log"
      summary+="$pkg: failed\n"
    fi
  fi
done < packages.txt
echo -e "$summary" | mailx -s "Package installation summary" admin@example.com

prompt: Monitor CPU usage every 5 seconds for 1 minute, output a table with timestamp, user, system, idle percentages, and alert if idle drops below 10 %.
command: end=$((SECONDS+60)); while [ $SECONDS -lt $end ]; do ts=$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S'); read user sys idle <<<$(mpstat 1 1 | awk '/Average/ {print $3,$5,$12}'); printf "%s | User: %s%% Sys: %s%% Idle: %s%%\n" "$ts" "$user" "$sys" "$idle"; if (( $(echo "$idle < 10" | bc -l) )); then echo "ALERT: Idle CPU below 10% at $ts"; fi; sleep 5; done

prompt: Create a Bash function called backup_dir that takes a directory path, creates a tar.gz archive named with the directory base and current date, stores it in /backups, and logs the operation to /var/log/backup.log.

prompt: List all Docker containers that have been stopped for more than 24 hours and remove them, printing each container ID before deletion.

prompt: Parse a JSON file config.json to extract the value of "service.port", then use curl to test if the service is reachable, retrying up to 3 times with exponential backoff.

prompt: Create a one‑liner that watches /var/log/auth.log for failed SSH login attempts, extracts the IP address, counts occurrences, and displays the top 3 offending IPs in real time.

prompt: Write a Bash script that reads a list of URLs from urls.txt, downloads each with curl (max 5 concurrent downloads), saves them with their original filename, and retries failed downloads up to 2 times.
command:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
xargs -a urls.txt -n1 -P5 -I{} bash -c '
  url="{}"
  fname=$(basename "$url")
  attempts=0
  while (( attempts < 3 )); do
    if curl -f -L -o "$fname" "$url"; then
      echo "Downloaded $fname"
      break
    else
      ((attempts++))
      echo "Retry $attempts for $url"
    fi
  done
'

prompt: Find all Git repositories under /srv, list their remote URLs, and check if the default branch is ahead of origin, printing repo path and status.
command: find /srv -type d -name .git -prune -print0 | while IFS= read -r -d '' gitdir; do repo=$(dirname "$gitdir"); cd "$repo" || continue; remote=$(git config --get remote.origin.url); default=$(git symbolic-ref refs/remotes/origin/HEAD | sed 's@^refs/remotes/origin/@@'); git fetch origin "$default" >/dev/null 2>&1; ahead=$(git rev-list --count "origin/$default..$default"); if (( ahead > 0 )); then echo "$repo | $remote | $default ahead by $ahead commits"; fi; done

prompt: Extract all IPv6 addresses from a mixed log file, normalize them to compressed form, count occurrences, and output the top 5.

prompt: Search recursively for all JSON files under /data, extract the field "user.id" using jq, count unique IDs, and output the top 3 most frequent IDs.

prompt: Write a script that backs up all MySQL databases, compresses each dump with xz, stores them in /backup/mysql with timestamps, and logs successes and failures to /var/log/mysql_backup.log.
command:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
log=/var/log/mysql_backup.log
mkdir -p /backup/mysql
mysql -e 'SHOW DATABASES;' -s --skip-column-names | while read db; do
  ts=$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S)
  dump="/backup/mysql/${db}_${ts}.sql"
  if mysqldump "$db" > "$dump"; then
    xz "$dump" && echo "$(date '+%F %T') SUCCESS $db" >> $log
  else
    echo "$(date '+%F %T') FAIL $db" >> $log
    rm -f "$dump"
  fi
done

prompt: Find all processes consuming more than 500 MB RSS, kill them gracefully, and if they persist after 10 seconds, force kill them, logging each action.

prompt: Write a Bash script that monitors the free space on /var, and when it falls below 5 GB, sends an email alert with a snapshot of the largest directories (top 5) using du.
command:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
threshold=5368709120
while true; do
  free=$(df --output=avail /var | tail -1 | tr -d ' ')
  if (( free < threshold )); then
    report=$(du -h --max-depth=1 /var | sort -hr | head -5)
    echo -e "Subject: Low Disk Space on /var\n\nFree space: $(numfmt --to=iec $free)\nTop directories:\n$report" | sendmail admin@example.com
  fi
  sleep 300
done

prompt: Create a Bash function that accepts a directory path and prints a tree of all symbolic links that point outside the given directory, showing the target absolute path.
Monitor CPU usage every 5 seconds for 1 minute, compute the average, and send an email alert if the average exceeds 80%. Assume mailx is configured.
command:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
samples=12
sum=0
for i in $(seq 1 $samples); do
  cpu=$(top -bn1 | grep "%Cpu(s)" | awk -F',' '{print $4}' | awk '{print $1}')
  sum=$(echo "$sum + $cpu" | bc)
  sleep 5
done
avg=$(echo "scale=2; $sum / $samples" | bc)
if (( $(echo "$avg > 80" | bc -l) )); then
  echo "Average CPU usage $avg% exceeds threshold" | mailx -s "CPU Alert" admin@example.com
fi

prompt: Create a Bash function that takes a git repository URL, clones it into /opt/repos if not present, pulls latest changes if it exists, and prints the latest commit hash.
command:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
update_repo(){
  local url=$1
  local name=$(basename "$url" .git)
  local dir=/opt/repos/$name
  if [[ -d $dir/.git ]]; then
    (cd "$dir" && git pull --quiet)
  else
    git clone --quiet "$url" "$dir"
  fi
  (cd "$dir" && git rev-parse HEAD)
}

prompt: List all open network ports with the owning process name, filter for ports > 1024, and output JSON array.

  port=$(echo "$addr" | awk -F':' '{print $NF}')

    printf '{"port":%s,"process":"%s"},' "$port" "$name"
  fi
done | sed 's/,$//' | awk '{print "["$0"]"}'

prompt: Write a Bash script that reads a list of URLs from urls.txt, downloads each with curl (max 5 retries, 10 s timeout), saves to /data with filenames based on SHA256 of the URL, and logs successes and failures.
command:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
log=/var/log/downloads.log
while read -r url; do
  fname=$(echo -n "$url" | sha256sum | cut -d' ' -f1)
  for i in {1..5}; do
    if curl -m 10 -sSL "$url" -o "/data/$fname"; then
      echo "$(date +%F_%T) SUCCESS $url -> $fname" >> $log; break

      echo "$(date +%F_%T) RETRY $i $url" >> $log
    fi
  done
  if (( i == 5 )); then
    echo "$(date +%F_%T) FAILURE $url" >> $log
  fi
done < urls.txt

prompt: Monitor CPU and memory usage of all processes owned by a given user every 10 seconds for 5 minutes, write the output to a timestamped CSV file, and generate a summary (average, max) at the end.

done

prompt: Find all symbolic links under /usr/local that are broken, replace each with a copy of the target file if it exists elsewhere in the filesystem, otherwise remove the link; log actions to /var/log/broken_links.log.
command:
find /usr/local -type l ! -exec test -e {} \; -print0 | while IFS= read -r -d '' link; do
  target=$(readlink "$link")
  real=$(find / -type f -name "$(basename "$target")" 2>/dev/null | head -n1)
  if [ -n "$real" ]; then
    cp --preserve=mode,ownership,timestamps "$real" "$(dirname "$link")/$(basename "$target")"

command:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
json_file="urls.json"
csv_out="results.csv"
echo "url,status,length" > "$csv_out"
jq -r '.[]' "$json_file" | while read -r url; do
  attempt=0
  success=0
  while (( attempt < 3 )); do
    ((attempt++))
    resp=$(curl -s -w "%{http_code} %{size_download}" -o /dev/null --max-time 5 "$url")
    code=$(echo "$resp" | awk '{print $1}')
    size=$(echo "$resp" | awk '{print $2}')
    if [[ $code -ge 200 && $code -lt 300 ]]; then
      echo ""$url",$code,$size" >> "$csv_out"
      success=1
      break
    fi
  done
  if (( success == 0 )); then
    echo "Failed to fetch $url after $attempt attempts" >&2
  fi
done

while docker events --filter 'event=start' --format '{{.ID}} {{.Image}} {{.Time}}' --since 0s; do
